definition_zh: 幸运地；侥幸地；幸好；好在
definition_en: by good chance; fortunately, especially because something bad was avoided
core_image: 躲过一劫后长出一口气：刚才差一点就出事
scene: 差一步就要踩到积水的台阶，好在突然停住了脚步。 I had already stepped out, but luckily there was a rail to catch.
sceneCN: 说话人差一点摔倒，最后抓住栏杆躲过一劫——这里 luckily 表示「幸好、侥幸躲过」（第 1 个义项：事情的结果偏向幸运一面）。

pos.zh: 幸运地；幸好（修饰整个句子）

derivatives.zh: 运气；幸运，luckily 的名词基础
幸运的；吉利的，luck 加形容词后缀 -y 而来
幸运；好运，形容词再加名词后缀 -ness

senses.title: Happening by good fortune
senses.definition: used to say that something good happened because of chance, not because anyone planned it
senses.definitionCN: 指某件好事因偶然机会发生，并非事先安排所致
senses.example: Luckily, the train was delayed, so we did not miss it.
senses.exampleCN: 幸好火车晚点了，我们才没错过。
senses.why: The adverb grows straight out of the noun luck: when luck works in your favor, the whole outcome turns out well.
senses.whyCN: 副词直接从名词 luck 长出来：运气站在你这一边，整个结果就朝好的方向发展。

senses.title: Escaping a bad result narrowly
senses.definition: used when something bad almost happened but was avoided by chance
senses.definitionCN: 指坏事几乎发生，却因偶然因素得以避免
senses.example: He fell off the ladder but luckily landed on a pile of leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 他从梯子上摔下来，但侥幸落在一堆树叶上。
senses.why: The core image is the near miss: luck intervenes at the last moment so the danger stays unreal.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是「差一点出事」：运气在最后一刻介入，危险始终没有成真。

senses.title: Adding a grateful comment to a statement
senses.definition: used at the start of a sentence to show relief that a situation was not worse
senses.definitionCN: 置于句首，表示庆幸情况没有更糟
senses.example: Luckily for us, the shop still had one ticket left.
senses.exampleCN: 对我们来说幸运的是，商店还剩一张票。
senses.why: English often turns adverbs into sentence-level comments; luckily works like fortunately to color the whole clause.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把副词用作整句的评注；luckily 和 fortunately 一样为整个句子染上庆幸的语气。

intro.en: Luckily is a young English adverb built directly on the noun luck, a word with northern Germanic roots.
intro.cn: luckily 是一个较年轻的英语副词，直接建立在名词 luck 之上，而 luck 源自北部日耳曼语。

items.en: The noun luck is generally traced to Old Norse happ, later a personal name Lukka, meaning chance or good fortune.
items.cn: 名词 luck 一般追溯到古诺斯语 happ（后作人名 Lukka），意为机会或好运。

items.en: Northern Dutch and Low German kept related forms such as luk, which helped carry the word into northern English speech.
items.cn: 荷兰北部与低地德语保留了 luk 等相关形式，帮助该词进入英格兰北部口语。

items.en: In Middle English luck meant fortune or chance, especially good fortune, and spread from the north to the whole country.
items.cn: 中古英语中 luck 意为运气或机会，尤指好运，并从北方扩散到全国。

items.en: The wider Germanic family links luck with words for happiness, since happ is also the source of happy.
items.cn: 更广的日耳曼语族把 luck 与「幸福」类词汇联系起来，因为 happ 同时也是 happy 的来源。

items.en: The adverb luckily formed in Modern English as luck plus the adverbial suffix -ly, first recorded in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 现代英语中 luckily 由 luck 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，最早见于十六世纪。

note.en: These neighbors either share luck as a base or compete with luckily in meaning.
note.cn: 这些邻近词要么共享词根 luck，要么在意义上与 luckily 相互竞争。

entries.definitionCN: 可指侥幸，也可指快乐地，语义更宽

entries.definitionCN: 习语：碰巧（可指好运也可指坏运）

normalIntro.en: Five ways to anchor luckily through its family and grammar.
normalIntro.cn: 从词族和语法两个角度记住 luckily 的五条线索。

normal.en: luck + -ly: turn the noun luck into an adverb.
normal.cn: luck 加副词后缀 -ly：把名词「运气」变成副词。

normal.en: lucky is the adjective pair; luckily is its adverb twin.
normal.cn: lucky 是形容词搭档，luckily 是它的副词孪生兄弟。

normal.en: Sentence adverb: luckily can stand at the front with a comma.
normal.cn: 作句首副词：luckily 可放在句首并用逗号隔开。

normal.en: Compare happily: luck and happ both mean good chance.
normal.cn: 对照 happily：luck 与 happ（幸福）本是同源意象。

normal.en: Frequently tells how often; luckily tells how the dice fell.
normal.cn: frequently 说频率，luckily 说骰子掷出的结果。

abstract.en: Picture a coin landing heads at the exact second you needed it.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币恰好在最需要的时刻正面朝上落地。

abstract.en: See a falling plate caught just before it hits the floor.
abstract.cn: 看见一个盘子坠向地面、在摔碎前一秒被接住。

abstract.en: Feel the relief in one long breath after the danger passes.
abstract.cn: 危险过后长长舒一口气的庆幸感。

examples.en: Luckily, the fire alarm rang before the smoke spread.
examples.cn: 幸好火警在烟雾蔓延前就响了。

examples.en: She had no umbrella, but luckily a stranger offered to share his.
examples.cn: 她没带伞，但幸好一位陌生人愿意与他共用。

examples.en: He guessed the last answer, and it turned out to be right.
examples.cn: 他猜了最后一道题的答案，结果竟然对了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉起利」——运气把人从坑里拉起来，自然有利：拉起来就幸运了。

root: luck 是英语北源的日耳曼词，一般认为借自古诺斯语 happ（机会、好运，亦为 happy 的来源），经低地德语区口语进入中古英语；luckily 在现代英语期加上副词后缀 -ly 构成。

sensesIntro.en: From plain good luck to narrow escapes and a grateful sentence comment.
sensesIntro.cn: 从单纯的好运，到惊险脱险，再到句首庆幸的语气词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a near miss that ends well
core.cn: 核心意象：差一点出事，结果却朝好的方向收场

branches.en: Good fortune makes the outcome positive.
branches.cn: 好运让结果转向好的一面。

branches.en: Danger almost lands but is dodged by chance.
branches.cn: 危险几乎落下来，却被偶然躲开。

branches.en: The speaker adds relief as a comment on the whole sentence.
branches.cn: 说话人把庆幸作为对整句的评注。

branches.en: Both senses rest on chance, not planning.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在偶然而非计划之上。

branches.en: A narrow escape naturally triggers the feeling of relief.
branches.cn: 惊险脱险自然引出庆幸之情。

intro.en: Luckily is built with a simple adverbial suffix on a Germanic noun base.
intro.cn: luckily 由日耳曼名词加简单副词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin has no direct role here, but parallel adverbs show the same pattern.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语在此并无直接参与，但平行的副词构造展现了相同模式。

items.meaning: in the manner of; turns adjectives into adverbs
items.meaningCN: 以……方式；把形容词变为副词
items.example: quickly means in a quick manner.
items.exampleCN: quickly 意为「以快速的方式」。

items.example: Luck was on our side today.
items.exampleCN: 今天运气站在我们这边。

items.example: The happy ending surprised no one.
items.exampleCN: 圆满结局没让任何人意外。

items.example: Fortunately, nobody was hurt.
Unluckily, the bus had just left.

items.structure: kin noun from the same Norse root

items.exampleCN: 一点小事故让开始时间推迟了。

items.example: Haply you will find it there.
items.exampleCN: 或许你能在那里找到它。

items.example: Perhaps the rain will stop soon.

definition_zh: 收到；接待；接收；受到
definition_en: to take into one's hands or possession; to welcome a guest; to pick up a signal; to experience something
core_image: 双手向前摊开，接住递来的东西
scene: 酒店门口，前台人员侧身让客人先进门。 The hotel receives guests from all over the world.
sceneCN: 这里 receives 是「接待」（第 2 个义项：迎接客人）；句意为这家酒店接待来自世界各地的客人。画面里可留意：门口侧身让路的前台、摊开的双手。

derivatives.zh: 接收器；听筒
接待；接收
收据
应收的

senses.title: To get what is sent
senses.definition: to take into one's hands or possession something that has been sent or given
senses.definitionCN: 把寄来或给予的东西拿到手中或归于自己
senses.example: She received a letter from her old teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 她收到了老教师寄来的一封信。
senses.why: Recipere joined re-, back, and capere, to take, so the word pictures taking something that comes to you.
senses.whyCN: recipere 由 re-（回）与 capere（拿取）组成，因此这个词描绘把送到你面前的东西收下。

senses.title: To welcome a guest
senses.definition: to greet and welcome someone who arrives
senses.definitionCN: 迎接并款待到来的人
senses.example: The hotel receives guests from all over the world.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店接待来自世界各地的客人。
senses.why: A guest is also something that comes to you, so the same verb covers taking a person in.
senses.whyCN: 客人也是来到你面前的人，因此同一个动词也涵盖把一个人迎进来。

senses.title: To pick up a signal
senses.definition: to catch and translate a broadcast or electronic signal
senses.definitionCN: 捕捉并转换广播或电子信号
senses.example: The old radio can still receive short-wave signals.
senses.exampleCN: 这台旧收音机仍能接收短波信号。
senses.why: A message arriving through the air is taken in by the set, so the same verb covers signals.
senses.whyCN: 通过空气传来的信息被机器收进来，因此同一个动词也用于信号。

senses.title: To experience something
senses.definition: to be given a reaction, a treatment, or an impression
senses.definitionCN: 得到某种反应、对待或印象
senses.example: The plan received strong criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案受到了强烈的批评。
senses.why: To receive a reaction is to have it delivered to you, even when the thing delivered is unpleasant.
senses.whyCN: 受到某种反应，就是让反应落到自己身上，即使落到身上的东西并不愉快。

intro.en: Receive is a Latin taking verb that came through French, and its image of open hands extends to guests, signals, and reactions.
intro.cn: receive 是经法语传来的拉丁「拿取」动词，其「摊开双手」的形象延伸到客人、信号与反应。

items.en: Capere meant to take or seize, the core of the whole family.
items.cn: capere 意为拿取或抓住，是整个词族的核心。

items.en: Recipere added re-, back, to capere, giving the sense of taking something in.
items.cn: recipere 在 capere 前加 re-（回），得到「把东西收进来」的意思。

items.en: Old French receivre carried the verb into English with its broad sense of taking.
items.cn: 古法语 receivre 把这个动词带入英语，保留了宽泛的「拿取」义。

items.en: Middle English receiven already covered letters, guests, and blows.
items.cn: 中古英语 receiven 已涵盖信件、客人，以及打击。

items.en: Modern English added signals and medical treatment to the older range.
items.cn: 现代英语在旧有范围上又加入了信号与医疗。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs ending in the same sound; the near-meaning group gathers words of getting and welcoming.
note.cn: 形近组收相同结尾音的动词；近义组收表获得与迎接的词。

entries.definition: To make someone believe what is false.
To form an idea or a plan.
To notice or understand something.
To take what is offered.
To get something, often with effort.
To come into possession of.
To greet a newcomer warmly.

normalIntro.en: The word pictures open hands: whatever comes, a letter or a guest, is taken in.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词描绘摊开的双手：无论来的是信还是客人，都被收进来。

normal.en: Re plus ceive: to take back what was sent to you.
normal.cn: re 加 ceive：把寄给你的东西收下来。

normal.en: Received is the past form, so write receive, received, receiving.
normal.cn: 过去式是 received，拼写为 receive、received、receiving。

normal.en: Receive guests is the formal way to say welcome them.
normal.cn: receive guests 是「迎接客人」的正式说法。

normal.en: A radio receives a signal with no hands at all.
normal.cn: 收音机接收信号，完全不用手。

normal.en: Receive criticism uses the same verb as receive a gift.
normal.cn: receive criticism 与 receive a gift 用的是同一个动词。

abstract.en: To receive is to accept that something comes from outside oneself.
abstract.cn: 接收就是承认有些东西来自自身之外。

abstract.en: A receiver must be open; a closed hand receives nothing.
abstract.cn: 接收者必须敞开，握紧的手什么也接不到。

abstract.en: Receiving a reaction is the price of having acted at all.
abstract.cn: 受到反应，是曾经行动过的代价。

examples.en: She received a letter from her old teacher.
examples.cn: 她收到了老教师寄来的一封信。

examples.en: The hotel receives guests from all over the world.
examples.cn: 这家酒店接待来自世界各地的客人。

examples.en: The plan received strong criticism.
examples.cn: 这个方案受到了强烈的批评。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（回）加 ceive（拿取）：把送来的东西拿回来，就是收到；把客人迎进来，就是接待。

sensesIntro.en: The core is taking something in; the senses move from things to guests, to signals, and to reactions.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把东西收进来」；义项从物品，到客人，到信号，再到反应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two open hands catching what is handed over.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只摊开的手接住递来的东西。

intro.cn: 这个词族建立在拉丁语的「拿取」动词上，前缀与英语后缀补充方向与施动者。

latinIntro.en: The Latin core is capere, to take, with re- meaning back; French carried it to English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁核心是 capere（拿取），前缀 re- 意为「回」；法语把它带到英语。

definition_zh: 使尴尬；使窘迫；使局促不安
definition_en: to make someone feel awkward, ashamed, or uncomfortable in front of others
core_image: 当众卡壳的脸：脸一下子红了，手脚都不知道往哪放
scene: 生日会上朋友突然唱起了他五岁的糗事歌。 The song embarrassed him in front of everyone.
sceneCN: 这里 embarrass 是「使尴尬」（第 1 个义项：使窘迫）；句意是那首歌让他在众人面前下不来台。图中可辨识物件：生日蛋糕、点歌的朋友、涨红的脸、捂脸的手。

derivatives.zh: 尴尬；窘迫
令人尴尬的
感到尴尬的

senses.title: To make someone feel awkward
senses.definition: to cause someone to feel self-conscious or ashamed
senses.definitionCN: 使某人难为情或羞愧。
senses.example: The song embarrassed him in front of everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 那首歌让他在众人面前下不来台。
senses.why: The old sense meant to block or hamper, and social blockage becomes the blush of shame.
senses.whyCN: 旧义为阻碍，社交受阻便化为羞赧脸红。

senses.title: To hinder or complicate
senses.definition: to make a plan or person unable to act freely
senses.definitionCN: 使计划或人无法自由行动。
senses.example: Debt embarrassed the young company.
senses.exampleCN: 债务让这家年轻公司举步维艰。
senses.why: The literal French sense of blocking a road survives in financial and formal writing.
senses.whyCN: 法语「堵路」的本义保留于财经与正式文体。

senses.title: To involve in financial difficulty
senses.definition: to burden a person or business with trouble, especially money trouble
senses.definitionCN: 使个人或企业陷入困境，尤指财务困难。
senses.example: He was embarrassed by unpaid bills.
senses.exampleCN: 未付的账单让他捉襟见肘。
senses.why: When a road is blocked, resources stop flowing, so money troubles use the same image.
senses.whyCN: 路被堵则资源断流，财务困境沿用同一意象。

intro.en: Embarrass began as a road-blocking image in French and Spanish.
intro.cn: embarrass 起于法语与西班牙语「堵路」的意象。

items.en: Spanish embarazar meant to obstruct, and also to make pregnant, a curious double life.
items.cn: 西班牙语 embarazar 意为阻碍，也有「使怀孕」的奇特义项。

items.en: French embarrasser kept the blocking sense: to bar the way.
items.cn: 法语 embarrasser 保留阻碍义：拦住去路。

items.en: The word combines em-, in, with the Portuguese baraça, a halter or strap.
items.cn: 该词由 em-（入内）加葡萄牙语 baraça（笼头、皮带）构成。

items.en: English borrowed it in the seventeenth century with the hampering sense.
items.cn: 英语于十七世纪借入，取其「妨碍」之义。

items.en: The social sense, to make someone blush, later became the dominant one.
items.cn: 「令人脸红」的社交义后来成为主导义项。

note.en: Two groups: spelling twins and the discomfort field.
note.cn: 两组：拼写孪生词与「不适」语义场。

senses.title: Belonging to the present age
senses.definition: of the present time or the recent past, as opposed to ancient times
senses.definitionCN: 属于当下或近期的，与古代相对
senses.example: Modern borders in this region were drawn less than a century ago.
senses.exampleCN: 这一地区的现代边界是不到一百年前划定的。
senses.why: Late Latin modernus was built from modo, just now, so the word first pointed at whatever belongs to the moment rather than at a fixed era.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁语 modernus 由 modo（就在此刻）构成，所以这个词原本指向属于当下那一刻的东西，而不是某个固定的时代。

senses.title: Using the newest methods or design
senses.definition: made with the latest techniques or materials, and therefore up to date
senses.definitionCN: 用最新技术或材料做成，因而跟得上时代
senses.example: The clinic replaced its old files with a modern records system.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所把旧档案换成了新式的记录系统。
senses.why: Anything of the present moment can be assumed to use present methods, so modern slid from a label of time to a label of technique.
senses.whyCN: 凡属于当下这一刻的东西，都可假定用了当下的办法，于是 modern 从时间标签滑成了技术标签。

senses.title: Of art that breaks with tradition
senses.definition: belonging to styles of art, music or architecture that deliberately abandon older rules
senses.definitionCN: 属于有意抛弃旧规矩的艺术、音乐或建筑风格
senses.example: The museum's modern wing puzzled visitors who expected marble columns.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的现代派展区让期待大理石柱的观众摸不着头脑。
senses.why: Artists who broke with the academy needed a name for their own work and took the word for the present age, so modern came to mean a deliberate break rather than a date.
senses.whyCN: 反叛学院派的艺术家需要给自家作品一个名号，便借用「当下时代」这个词，于是 modern 指一次有意的断裂，而不只是标一个日期。

senses.title: Open rather than old-fashioned in outlook
senses.definition: willing to accept new ideas about family, work or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 在家事、工作或行为上愿意接受新观念
senses.example: Her modern attitude toward housework surprised her grandparents.
senses.exampleCN: 她对家务的现代态度让祖父母吃惊。
senses.why: If modern means of this moment, a person who keeps up with the moment is called modern in temper, and the word becomes mild praise for being unshackled from old habits.
senses.whyCN: 如果 modern 指「属于此刻」，那么跟上此刻的人就被称为性情 modern；这个词就这样变成了对「不被旧习惯捆住」的一种温和赞许。

intro.en: Modern goes back to Late Latin modernus, formed from modo, just now, plus a suffix of time; it reached English through French and was first used to contrast the present with the ancient world.
intro.cn: modern 可追到晚期拉丁语 modernus，它由 modo（就在此刻）加一个时间后缀构成；经法语进入英语，最初用来把当下与古代世界对照。

items.en: Modo was an adverb meaning just now or only a moment ago, and it supplied the seed of the word for what belongs to the present.
items.cn: modo 是一个副词，意为「就在此刻、刚才」，它为表示「属于当下」的词提供了种子。

items.en: Modernus is usually dated to the fifth century and was built with the time suffix also seen in hodiernus, of today; its coinage is generally thought to set the present against the ancient past.
items.cn: modernus 一般被认为出现于五世纪，用的是与 hodiernus（今天的）相同的时间后缀；一般认为，这个新造词把当下与古代对立起来。

items.en: French used moderne for what belonged to the current age and passed the word to English in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语用 moderne 指属于当前时代的东西，并在十六世纪把这个词传入英语。

items.en: English modern first joined the quarrel of the ancients and the moderns, where it meant the writers and scholars of recent times.
items.cn: 英语的 modern 最早出现在「古代人与现代人之争」里，当时指近代的作家与学者。

items.en: Modern English extended the word to technology, to a style of art that rejects old rules, and to people whose views keep pace with the age.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词扩展到技术、反叛旧规矩的艺术风格，以及观念跟得上时代的人。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a timestamp built on the Latin adverb for just now, and its family keeps dividing into state, action, movement and believer.

normal.en: Modo, Latin for just now, is the root of modern, so the word is a timestamp before it is a style.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 modo 意为「就在此刻」，它是 modern 的词根，所以这个词先是一个时间戳，然后才是一种风格。

normal.en: The suffix that made modernus belongs to the same time-naming kind as the one in hodiernus, of today, which is why the word reads as belonging to now.
normal.cn: 造出 modernus 的那个后缀，与 hodiernus（今天的）里的时间后缀同类，所以这个词读起来就是「属于现在」。

normal.en: Add -ity for the condition, -ize for the act of updating, -ism for the movement, -ist for the person, so one stem covers state, action, style and believer.
normal.cn: 加 -ity 表状态，加 -ize 表更新的动作，加 -ism 表流派，加 -ist 表人，一个词干覆盖状态、动作、风格与信奉者。

normal.en: Postmodern adds post- to modern, marking a reaction against the very style that modern had named.
normal.cn: postmodern 在 modern 前加 post-，标出对 modern 曾经命名的那种风格的反动。

normal.en: The ancients and the moderns were a real quarrel in European letters, and English modern kept the flavour of taking sides in that argument.

normal.cn: injustice 最能体现词根本义：不公。

abstract.en: One image: a bandage that can wrap an arm, a purse or a name.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：绷带能缠手臂、钱袋，也能缠名字。

abstract.en: Injure is a wrong step against someone.
abstract.cn: injure 是对某人踏错的一步。

abstract.en: The scales tip and someone bleeds.
abstract.cn: 天平一斜，就有人流血。

examples.en: She injured her ankle on the stairs.
examples.cn: 她在楼梯上扭伤了脚踝。

examples.en: No one was injured in the fire.
examples.cn: 火灾中无人受伤。

examples.en: The false story injured his good name.
examples.cn: 虚假报道损害了他的名誉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「因哲」：因为不义之举，让人「折」了筋骨， injure。

root: 拉丁语 in-「不」+ jus/juris「法律、正当」→ injuria「不义」→ injuriare「行不义」→ 古法语 injurier → 中古英语 injuren；本义「不义对待」，后扩展至身体伤害；同根词 justice、jury、judge。

sensesIntro.en: Injure is a bandage: it wraps a hurt leg, a hurt purse, a hurt name, and a limping cause.
sensesIntro.cn: injure 是一条绷带：缠住伤腿、受损的钱袋、受伤的名声，以及跛行的事业。

core.en: A wrong done against right, leaving the body, purse or name bandaged.
core.cn: 违逆正当而行的错，让身体、钱财或名声缠上绷带。

branches.en: LOSS: the delay injured small businesses.
branches.cn: 损失：延误损害了小企业。

branches.en: DAMAGE: bad reporting injured the inquiry.
branches.cn: 损害：糟糕报道损害调查。

branches.en: WOUNDING: harm on body or heart.
branches.cn: 致伤：对身体或心灵的伤害。

intro.en: Injure builds injury, injured and injurious beside the law family.
intro.cn: injure 构成 injury、injured、injurious，并与法律词族相伴。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the right-law noun jus behind the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示词族背后的正当法律名词 jus。

items.example: Smoke can injure the lungs.
The injury kept him out for weeks.
The injured were taken to hospital.
Injurious chemicals leaked.
They fought against injustice.
Justice was finally done.
The jury reached a verdict.
Old prejudice dies hard.

latinEntries.meaning: law, right, that which is due

definition_zh: 劳动；工作；劳动力；工党；分娩
definition_en: physical or mental work, especially hard work; also the workforce as a group and the process of giving birth
core_image: 两只手紧握工具，把力气一点点变成看得见的成果
scene: 天还没亮，工地上的灯已经亮起，工人们把沉重的沙袋一袋袋扛上肩。 After a long day of labour, the crew sat down beside the unfinished wall.
sceneCN: 这里是「劳动、劳作」（第 1 个义项：付出体力的工作）；句意为干了一整天活之后，工人们坐在未完工的墙边歇下。图中可辨识物件：工地灯、沙袋、半截砖墙。

derivatives.zh: 由 labour 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「劳动者；工人」
由拉丁词干 labor 加 -ious 构成，义为「费力的；艰苦的」
由 labour 与 intensive 复合而成，义为「劳动密集型的」

senses.title: Physical work, especially of a hard kind
senses.definition: work, especially hard physical work, done with effort over time
senses.definitionCN: 尤指需要长时间付出体力的艰苦工作
senses.example: The wall was built through months of hard labour.
senses.exampleCN: 这堵墙是经过数月苦干才砌成的。
senses.why: Latin labor meant toil and hardship, so the word starts from the strain felt in the body rather than from the finished product.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 labor 本义是「辛劳、艰苦」，所以这个词的起点是身体感到的吃力，而不是最后完成的成果。

senses.title: The workforce as a group
senses.definition: the people who work, considered as a whole, especially in an industry or country
senses.definitionCN: 把从事工作的人作为一个整体来看，尤指某一行业或国家的劳动力
senses.example: The factory needs more skilled labour.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂需要更多技术工人。
senses.why: Once labour names the effort, it can also name the people who supply that effort, which is why the word shifts from activity to a collective body.
senses.whyCN: 既然 labour 能指付出的力气，也就能指提供这些力气的人，于是词义从「活动」转到「集体的人群」。

senses.title: Organized political labour
senses.titleCN: 工党；有组织的劳工运动
senses.definition: the political party or movement that represents the interests of workers
senses.definitionCN: 代表工人利益的政治党派或有组织的运动
senses.example: He voted for Labour in the last election.
senses.exampleCN: 上次选举他投了工党的票。
senses.why: When workers organize, the same word moves from the shop floor to the ballot box, naming the political force built on their shared interests.
senses.whyCN: 当工人联合起来，同一个词就从车间走向投票箱，用来指建立在他们共同利益之上的政治力量。

senses.title: Childbirth
senses.definition: the process of giving birth, especially the final stage with strong contractions
senses.definitionCN: 生育的过程，尤指伴随强烈宫缩的最后阶段
senses.example: She went into labour at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 她在黎明时开始分娩。
senses.why: Childbirth is the hardest bodily work a person can do, so English borrowed the word for toil to describe it, keeping the sense of intense physical effort.
senses.whyCN: 分娩是人身体上最吃力的一种劳作，英语便借「辛苦出力」这个词来描述它，保留了强烈体力付出的意味。

intro.en: Labour is a Latin word for toil that travelled through French before it named work, workers and birth in English.
intro.cn: labour 是拉丁语中表示「辛劳」的词，经法语进入英语，先指干活，再指劳动者与分娩。

items.en: Labor meant toil, hardship and effort, and it could also name the fruit of that effort.
items.cn: labor 意为辛劳、艰苦、出力，也可指付出之后得到的成果。

items.en: The verb laborare meant to work or to struggle, and it supplied the family of words about effort.
items.cn: 动词 laborare 意为干活、挣扎，派生出一整族与出力有关的词。

items.en: Old French took the noun as labour, meaning work or task, and passed it to English after the Norman conquest.
items.cn: 古法语把名词写作 labour，意为工作、活儿，诺曼征服之后传入英语。

items.en: Middle English labour covered both the act of working and the trouble or hardship that came with it.
items.cn: 中古英语的 labour 同时指干活这件事和随之而来的辛苦、磨难。

items.en: Modern English keeps the British spelling labour and the American labor, and extends the word to workers, their party and childbirth.
items.cn: 现代英语保留英式 labour 与美式 labor 两种拼写，并把词义扩展到劳动者、工党与分娩。

note.en: The look-alike group collects spellings and relatives built on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group collects words for work and effort.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的拼写与同族词；近义组收表示工作与出力的词。

entries.definition: The American spelling of labour, with the same meanings.
entries.definitionCN: labour 的美式拼写，含义完全相同。

entries.definition: Needing a lot of time and effort to do.
entries.definitionCN: 需要花费大量时间与力气的；费力的。

entries.definition: A room or building used for scientific work.
entries.definitionCN: 用于科学工作的房间或建筑；实验室。

entries.definition: To work together with someone on a task.
entries.definitionCN: 与某人合作完成一项任务。

entries.definition: Activity done to achieve a purpose, often as a job.
entries.definitionCN: 为达到目的而从事的活动，常指工作。

entries.definition: Long, hard and tiring work.
entries.definitionCN: 长时间、艰苦而累人的劳动。

entries.definition: The energy spent trying to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 为做某事而付出的精力。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin stem for toil, and its family keeps returning to effort, hardship and the people who do the work.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示「辛劳」的拉丁词干上，同族词反复回到出力、艰苦以及干活的人。

normal.en: Labor in Latin means toil, so labour is not just work but work that costs the body something.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 labor 意为辛劳，所以 labour 不只是工作，而是让身体付出代价的活。

normal.en: Labourer adds -er to labour: the person who does the labour.
normal.cn: labourer 在 labour 后加 -er，就是「干活的人」。

normal.en: Laborious adds -ious to the same stem: full of labour, therefore tiring.
normal.cn: laborious 在同一词干后加 -ious，意为「充满劳作的」，因此是费力的。

normal.en: The British spelling has a u, the American spelling drops it, just like colour and color.
normal.cn: 英式拼写带 u，美式去掉 u，就像 colour 与 color 一样。

normal.en: Labour Party is capitalized because it names a political party, not work in general.
normal.cn: Labour Party 首字母大写，因为它指一个政党，而不是泛指劳动。

abstract.en: A single word for effort, workers and birth suggests that English treats all three as kinds of hard work.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时表示出力、劳动者和分娩，说明英语把这三者都看成某种辛苦的劳作。

abstract.en: When a word moves from the body to the ballot box, the same strain is being organized into power.
abstract.cn: 当一个词从身体走向投票箱，同样的辛苦被组织成了力量。

abstract.en: Labour is a reminder that behind every finished thing there is a stretch of time that somebody had to endure.
abstract.cn: labour 提醒人：每件完成的东西背后，都有一段有人必须熬过去的时间。

examples.en: The wall was built through months of hard labour.
examples.cn: 这堵墙是经过数月苦干才砌成的。

examples.en: The country's labour force is growing older.
examples.cn: 这个国家的劳动力正在老龄化。

examples.en: She was in labour for six hours.
examples.cn: 她分娩持续了六个小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累吧」——活儿干多了，人就会喊着累吧；记住 labour 是劳动。

root: 拉丁语 labor（劳作、辛苦）经古法语 labour 进入英语；同族词多与「干活、费力气」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is effortful work; the senses then divide into the people who work, their political party, and the hardest bodily work of all.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是费力的工作；义项由此分出干活的人、代表他们的政党，以及最吃力的身体劳作——分娩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands gripping a tool and turning effort into a visible result.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手紧握工具，把力气一点点变成看得见的成果。

branches.en: a wall rising slowly under a hot sun
branches.cn: 烈日下一寸寸升起的墙

branches.en: a worker counting the hours until the shift ends
branches.cn: 工人数着还有多久下工

branches.en: a factory hiring more hands for the season
a ballot box standing in for the shop floor
a family waiting outside a delivery room

intro.en: The word is held together by a Latin noun of toil, its verb, and two English suffixes that turn it into a person and a quality.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示辛劳的拉丁名词、它的动词，以及两个把它变成「人」和「性质」的英语后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 增加；增长；增多的量
definition_en: to become larger in amount or number, or the amount by which something grows
core_image: 温度计的水银柱慢慢往上升
scene: 城市年年盖起更多高楼。 The number of visitors will increase this summer.
sceneCN: 这里 increase 是动词「增加」（第 1 个义项：数量变大）；句意：今年夏天游客数量将增加。

derivatives.zh: increase 加副词后缀，义为「越来越；日益」
increase 加过去分词后缀，义为「增加了的」
加反义前缀 de-，义为「减少」

senses.title: To grow larger in number
senses.definition: to become larger in amount, number or degree
senses.definitionCN: 在数量、数目或程度上变大
senses.example: Sales increased by twenty percent.
senses.exampleCN: 销量增长了百分之二十。
senses.why: A rising column on the meter shows the growth.
senses.whyCN: 仪表上不断升高的读数显示出增长。

senses.title: To make something larger
senses.definition: to cause something to become larger
senses.definitionCN: 使某物变大变多
senses.example: They increased the dose carefully.
senses.exampleCN: 他们谨慎地加大了剂量。
senses.why: A hand pushes the column higher on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 一只手刻意把读数推得更高。

senses.title: The amount of growth
senses.definition: the amount by which something has grown
senses.definitionCN: 某物增长的量
senses.example: There was a sharp increase in fares.
senses.exampleCN: 票价急剧上涨。
senses.why: The column rise itself gets a name.
senses.whyCN: 水银柱的上升本身也得了名字。

senses.title: Steady ongoing growth
senses.definition: growth that continues over time
senses.definitionCN: 随时间延续的增长
senses.example: The city has seen a steady increase in traffic.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市的交通量持续增长。
senses.why: The meter climbs season after season.
senses.whyCN: 仪表一季一季地攀升。

intro.en: Increase comes from Latin increscere, from in- (in, toward) + crescere (to grow). The picture is growth moving upward from inside.
intro.cn: increase 来自拉丁语 increscere，由 in-「向内」+ crescere「生长」构成，画面是自内而上的生长。

items.en: Latin crescere meant to grow, to spring up; it also gave crescent and crescendo.
items.cn: 拉丁语 crescere 意为生长、萌发；同根词还有 crescent 与 crescendo。

items.en: in- plus crescere formed increscere: to grow in, to grow toward.
items.cn: in- 加 crescere 构成 increscere：向内生长、逐渐增多。

items.en: The word passed through Old French increistre.
items.cn: 该词经古法语 increistre 传入。

items.en: Middle English encresen kept both the verb and the noun uses.
items.cn: 中古英语 encresen 同时保留动词与名词用法。

items.en: Modern English fixed the noun stress on the first syllable: an increase.
items.cn: 现代英语把名词重音固定在第一音节：an increase。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the grow-root family and its opposite. The meaning group compares words of rising numbers.
note.cn: 形近组收录「生长」词根词族及其反义词；词义组比较表示数量上升的词。

entries.definition: to become smaller, the direct antonym.
a gradual rise in sound, from the same Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 声音渐强，同出拉丁词根。

entries.definition: spelling neighbor with a different origin.
to become larger naturally.
to go up in level or amount.
to spread out to a larger size.

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the grow root, the percent phrase and the stress switch.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩利用「生长」词根、百分比短语与重音变化。

normal.en: in- plus crescere (grow): growth moving inward and upward.
normal.cn: in- 加 crescere（生长）：向内向上生长。

normal.en: Verb stress is IN-crease later; noun stress is IN-crease first: an increase.
normal.cn: 动词重音在后，名词重音在前：an increase。

normal.en: increase by ten percent is the exam favorite.
normal.cn: increase by ten percent 是考试常客。

normal.en: decrease is the twin with de- going down.
normal.cn: decrease 是带 de- 的下行孪生词。

normal.en: crescendo in music is the same idea of rising.
normal.cn: 音乐里的 crescendo 渐强是同一个上升概念。

abstract.en: One image: mercury climbing a thermometer.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：水银在温度计里攀升。

abstract.en: Every increase begins as one small seed of growth.
abstract.cn: 每次增长都始于一粒生长的种子。

abstract.en: Numbers are water: they rise when poured in.
abstract.cn: 数字像水：倒进去就上涨。

examples.en: House prices increased sharply last year.
examples.cn: 去年房价急剧上涨。

examples.en: We need to increase production to meet demand.
examples.cn: 我们需要增产以满足需求。

examples.en: There has been a big increase in online orders.
examples.cn: 线上订单大幅增长。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「因克瑞斯」：因为加了克数，瑞祥上升， increase。

root: 拉丁语 in-「向内」+ crescere「生长」→ increscere「逐渐增多」→ 古法语 increistre → 中古英语 encresen → 现代英语 increase；同根词 crescent、crescendo、decrease。

sensesIntro.en: Increase is the climbing meter: numbers going up, hands pushing them up, the rise itself, and growth that will not stop.
sensesIntro.cn: increase 是攀升的仪表：数字上涨、人手推升、上涨本身，以及不停歇的增长。

core.en: A rising column that measures growth in numbers, size and force.
core.cn: 一根不断升高的读数柱，量出数量、规模与力度的增长。

branches.en: NUMBERS: sales increased by twenty percent.
MEASURE: a sharp increase in fares.
TREND: a steady increase in traffic.

branches.cn: 规模：随时间量出的增长。

intro.en: Increase builds increased, increasing, increasingly and its twin decrease.
intro.cn: increase 构成 increased、increasing、increasingly 及孪生词 decrease。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the growth verb crescere behind the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示词族背后的生长动词 crescere。

items.example: Costs increased again.
Increased demand raised prices.
Increasing crowds filled the hall.
items.exampleCN: 越来越多的人群挤满大厅。

items.example: It is increasingly common.
The noise decreased at night.
A crescent hung in the sky.
The music reached a crescendo.
Interest accrues monthly.

definition_zh: 满的；完整的；充分的；吃饱的；最大的
definition_en: containing as much as possible, complete, or reaching the greatest amount or degree
core_image: 一只倒满的杯子，水面贴着杯沿将溢未溢
scene: 茶壶咕嘟作响，热气漫过桌布。 She poured until each cup was full, then set the teapot down.
sceneCN: 这里 full 是「满的」（第 1 个义项：装到不能再装）；句意为她把每只杯子倒得满满的才放下茶壶。

pos.zh: 满的；充满的；完整的；充分的
完全地；整整（常与 -ly 连用或直接修饰）

derivatives.zh: full 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「完全地；充分地」
与 full 同源的日耳曼动词，义为「装满；填满」
full + fill 的组合动词，义为「履行；实现」

senses.title: Containing as much as possible
senses.definition: holding or containing as much as it can
senses.definitionCN: 装着或容纳尽可能多的东西
senses.example: The hall was full long before the concert began.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐会还没开始大厅就坐满了。
senses.why: The image is a container at its limit, so this is the base sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 画面是容器到达极限，这是词的基础义项。

senses.title: Complete, with nothing missing
senses.definition: including everything; not shortened or partial
senses.definitionCN: 包含全部，没有缩减或缺省
senses.example: Please write your full address on the form.
senses.exampleCN: 请在表格上写完整地址。
senses.why: A full container has no empty space; a full account has no missing part, so completeness extends the container image.
senses.whyCN: 满的容器没有空隙，完整的叙述没有缺漏，因此「完整」扩展了容器画面。

senses.title: Greatest amount or degree
senses.definition: as great, high, or much as possible
senses.definitionCN: 达到尽可能大的程度或数量
senses.example: The bus turned at full speed round the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 巴士全速转过街角。
senses.why: Degree is treated like a container filled to the top, so maximum degree reuses the image.
senses.whyCN: 程度被当作装满的容器来想象，于是「最高程度」复用该画面。

senses.title: Having eaten enough
senses.definition: feeling that you have eaten enough food
senses.definitionCN: 吃了足够的食物之后的饱腹感
senses.example: The children said they were too full for dessert.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们说太饱了，吃不下甜点。
senses.why: The stomach is imagined as a small container that can be filled, so fullness of food reuses the base image.
senses.whyCN: 胃被想象成可填满的小容器，因此「吃饱」复用基础画面。

senses.title: Completely busy or occupied
senses.definition: filled with planned activities or work
senses.definitionCN: 被安排的活动或工作占满
senses.example: Her diary is full until the end of the month.
senses.exampleCN: 她的日程本排到了月底。
senses.why: Time slots behave like container space, so a busy schedule is a filled one.
senses.whyCN: 时间段如同容器空间，因此排满的日程就是「满」的日程。

senses.title: Wide, with a rounded shape
senses.definition: made with extra width or a rounded shape, as of clothing
senses.definitionCN: 衣物做得宽大或带圆弧形状
senses.example: The dancer wore a full skirt that swirled.
senses.exampleCN: 舞者穿着会旋转飞舞的宽摆裙。
senses.why: A garment filled out with fabric looks round and ample, borrowing the filled image for shape.
senses.whyCN: 被布料撑起来的衣物显得圆润丰盈，借「充满」的画面描述形状。

intro.en: Full is a native Germanic adjective whose root also gave fill and many -ful suffixes.
intro.cn: full 是日耳曼本土形容词，其词根同时派生出 fill 与众多 -ful 后缀。

items.en: A Germanic root *ful- meant full, complete.
items.cn: 日耳曼词根 *ful- 表示「满的、完整的」。

items.en: Old English full meant full and complete, already in wide use.
items.cn: 古英语 full 表示「满的、完整的」，已广泛使用。

items.en: The related verb fyllan, to fill, came from the same root family.
items.cn: 同源动词 fyllan（装满）出自同一词根族。

items.en: Middle English full kept both container and completeness senses.
items.cn: 中古英语 full 保留容器义与完整义。

items.en: Modern English full also produced the suffix -ful, meaning full of.
items.cn: 现代英语 full 还产出了后缀 -ful，意为「充满……的」。

note.en: Full is short and common, so it collides with several short look-alikes.
note.cn: full 短小常用，与多个短形近词相撞。

entries.definition: having all necessary parts

normal.en: Full is the adjective state, fill is the verb action: the state versus the act.
normal.cn: full 是形容词表状态，fill 是动词表动作：状态与动作相对。

normal.en: The suffix -ful grew out of full, so hopeful means full of hope.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ful 由 full 脱落而来，hopeful 即充满希望。

normal.en: The collocation be full of is the most frequent, so learn it first.
normal.cn: 搭配 be full of 最高频，先把它记牢。

normal.en: Feel full covers the everyday scene of finishing a meal.
normal.cn: feel full 覆盖了吃完一顿饭的日常场景。

normal.en: In full means paying or reading everything, nothing held back.
normal.cn: in full 指全额付清或全文读出，毫不保留。

abstract.en: Watch water rise to the brim, one drop short of spilling.
abstract.cn: 看水位涨到杯沿，再一滴就会溢出。

abstract.en: See a diary with every line written in: that schedule is full.
abstract.cn: 想象一页写满的日程本：这就是 full。

abstract.en: Full and fool differ by one o, separating wisdom from silliness.
abstract.cn: full 与 fool 只差一个 o，一个饱满一个痴傻。

definition_zh: 清晰地；明显地；无疑地；清楚地
definition_en: in a way easy to see, hear or understand; without doubt
core_image: 噪声散去后，那句话听得一清二楚
scene: 教室后排的耳机坏了，我把音量调到最大。 I could clearly hear the teacher's question.
sceneCN: 这里 clearly 是「清晰地」（第 1 个义项：容易听清、看清的方式）；句意是我能清楚地听到老师的问题。

senses.title: In a way easy to perceive
senses.definition: so that something can be seen, heard or understood easily
senses.definitionCN: 以容易被看到、听到或理解的方式
senses.example: Please read the word clearly and slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 请把这个词读得清晰而缓慢。
senses.why: The basic use describes how the act of perceiving succeeds.
senses.whyCN: 基本用法描述感知得以顺利完成的方式。

senses.title: Without doubt; obviously
senses.definition: used to say something is easy to be sure about
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示某事毫无疑问
senses.example: He is clearly the best runner in our class.
senses.exampleCN: 他显然是我们班跑得最快的人。
senses.why: When nothing blocks judgement, the truth stands out.
senses.whyCN: 毫无遮挡时，事实一目了然，义项由此而来。

senses.title: With a clear mind or manner
senses.definition: thinking or speaking in an organized, direct way
senses.definitionCN: 以有条理、直接的方式思考或表达
senses.example: Think clearly before you answer.
senses.exampleCN: 回答前先把思路理清。
senses.why: An unblocked mind works like an unblocked road.
senses.whyCN: 畅通的头脑如同畅通的道路。

intro.en: Clearly is clear plus the everyday adverb maker -ly.
intro.cn: clearly 就是 clear 加上常用副词后缀 -ly。

items.en: Latin clarus meant bright and evident.
items.cn: 拉丁语 clarus 义为明亮、显然。

items.en: Old French carried it as cler.
items.cn: 古法语作 cler 传入。

items.en: Middle English used clere as both adjective and adverb.
items.cn: 中古英语 clere 兼作形容词和副词。

items.en: Middle English built adverbs with the ending -lic, later -ly.
items.cn: 中古英语用词尾 -lic（后来的 -ly）构成副词。

items.en: Modern English fixed the form as clearly.
items.cn: 现代英语定型为 clearly。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alikes; the second gathers obvious words.
note.cn: 第一组收形近词，第二组收明显类词。

entries.definition: A person or product that cleans.

entries.definition: Easy to see or understand.

entries.definition: More clear.
In a way easy to notice.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「显然」，与 clearly 的无疑义相近。

entries.definition: In a simple, direct way.
In a way easy to tell apart.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「清楚地；明显地」。

normalIntro.en: Remember clearly as clear plus -ly.

normal.en: -ly turns adjectives into adverbs.

normal.en: clear is the base; clearly its adverb.

normal.en: speak clearly helps listeners.

normal.en: clearly wrong means obviously wrong.

abstract.cn: 仿佛听见乐队中一个干净的音符浮起。

abstract.en: See a straight path with no fog on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条没有雾气的笔直小路。

abstract.en: Feel the nod of agreement when the point lands.
abstract.cn: 感受道理讲透时对方点头认同的瞬间。

examples.cn: 说明书写得很清楚。

examples.en: She clearly explained the rule to us.
examples.cn: 她清楚地向我们解释了规则。

examples.en: Clearly, more practice is needed.
examples.cn: 显然还需要更多练习。

root: clear（拉丁语 clarus，明亮清晰）+ -ly（古英语 -lic，副词后缀）→ 中古英语 clere → 现代英语 clearly；同根词有 clarity、clarify、declare。

sensesIntro.en: Clearly describes easy perception, sure facts and organized thinking.

definition_zh: 嘿；喂（用于引起注意或打招呼）
definition_en: used to call attention or to greet someone informally
core_image: 隔着人群喊出的那一声招呼
scene: 操场上球飞出界外，同学们齐声喊住捡球的男孩，让他别走远。 Hey, come back! The ball rolled this way, not that way.
sceneCN: 这里 hey 是「引起注意」（第 1 个义项：呼唤提醒）；同学们喊住男孩，让他注意球滚来的方向。

senses.title: To call attention
senses.definition: used to make someone notice you or something
senses.definitionCN: 用来让某人注意你或某件事
senses.example: Hey, you dropped your wallet on the floor!
senses.exampleCN: 嘿，你的钱包掉在地上了！
senses.why: A shout must be short and loud; hey is the shortest way to grab an ear.
senses.whyCN: 呼喊必须短促有力，hey 是抓住耳朵的最短方式。

senses.title: An informal greeting
senses.definition: used as a friendly, casual hello between people
senses.definitionCN: 熟人之间随口友好的问候
senses.example: Hey, long time no see! How have you been?
senses.exampleCN: 嗨，好久不见！最近怎么样？
senses.why: The same shout softens into a greeting when the meeting is friendly.
senses.whyCN: 同样的喊声在友好相遇时软化为问候。

senses.title: To show surprise or protest
senses.definition: used to show that you are surprised or annoyed
senses.definitionCN: 表示惊讶或轻微抗议的语气词
senses.example: Hey! That is my seat, not yours.
senses.exampleCN: 嘿！那是我的座位，不是你的。
senses.why: A shout that grabs attention also marks boundaries when something is wrong.
senses.whyCN: 引起注意的喊声在不对劲时也能标出界限。

intro.en: Hey is one of the oldest natural cries in English.
intro.cn: hey 是英语中最古老的天然呼喊声之一。

items.en: Middle English spelled it hei, hai, hey, used to call attention.
items.cn: 中古英语拼作 hei、hai、hey，用于呼唤注意。

items.en: The Middle English cry probably echoes Old French haï, itself a call.
items.cn: 中古英语的呼喊可能呼应古法语 haï，本身也是一种呼唤。

items.en: Similar cries appear across Germanic languages, such as German hei.
items.cn: 日耳曼诸语言都有类似呼喊，如德语 hei。

items.en: American English made hey a common casual greeting in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 二十世纪美国英语让 hey 成为常见的随口问候。

items.en: Because it imitates a natural shout, the deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 由于它模仿天然喊声，更深的来源不确定。

note.en: Compare hey with other greeting shouts.
note.cn: 把 hey 与其他招呼声对照。

normalIntro.cn: 把 hey 绑定在日常喊人场景里。

normal.en: hey and hay sound the same but hay is grass.
normal.cn: hey 与 hay 同音，hay 是干草——别喊错了。

normal.en: Hey, hi, hello: three levels of casual greetings.
normal.cn: hey、hi、hello：三种随意问候，一个比一个正式。

normal.en: Use hey to stop someone: Hey, wait!
normal.cn: 用 hey 叫停别人：Hey, wait!（嘿，等等）。

normal.en: Middle English hei has kept the same sound.

normal.en: Hey there is a friendly opener in messages.

abstract.cn: 想象你高举一只手臂喊 hey 的画面。

abstract.en: Feel hey as a small stone thrown into a noisy crowd.
abstract.cn: 把 hey 感受成扔进喧闹人群的小石子——立刻引来目光。

abstract.en: Hear two friends call hey across the street.
abstract.cn: 听见两个朋友隔街互喊 hey 的声音。

examples.en: Hey, did you see the new student in our class?
examples.cn: 嘿，你看到我们班的新同学了吗？

examples.en: Hey! Mind the wet paint on the bench.
examples.cn: 嘿！注意长椅上油漆未干。

examples.en: He gave a hey of surprise when the lights went out.
examples.cn: 灯熄灭时他惊讶地喊了一声嘿。

sensesIntro.en: One short cry grows three uses: calling, greeting, protesting.
sensesIntro.cn: hey 的一声呼喊长出三种用法：唤人、问候、抗议。

definition_zh: 习惯；习性；（修士的）道袍
definition_en: something you do often and regularly, often without thinking about it
core_image: 每天清晨闹钟一响就伸手按掉然后起床，动作全自动不假思索
scene: 连续一个月每天睡前刷牙后，小林不看提醒也会自动走进洗手间。 Reading before bed is a good habit for students.
sceneCN: 这里 habit 是「习惯」（第 1 个义项：不假思索反复做的事）；句意是睡前阅读对学生们是个好习惯。

derivatives.zh: 由 habit 加 -ual 构成，义为「习惯性的；惯常的」
由 habitual 加 -ly 构成，义为「习惯性地」

senses.title: A repeated personal action
senses.definition: an action repeated so often that it becomes automatic
senses.definitionCN: 反复多次以致自动化的行为
senses.example: Biting nails is a nervous habit.
senses.exampleCN: 咬指甲是紧张时的习惯。
senses.why: The alarm-clock picture shows action without thought, which is the core of the sense.
senses.whyCN: 闹钟一响就自动起床的画面，正是「不假思索地做」这一核心。

senses.title: A tendency of animals or plants
senses.definition: the usual behavior of an animal or growth pattern of a plant
senses.definitionCN: 动物的一贯行为或植物的生长习性
senses.example: Owls have nocturnal habits.
senses.exampleCN: 猫头鹰有夜间活动的习性。
senses.why: If people repeat, nature repeats too; the same loop covers species.
senses.whyCN: 人会重复，自然界的物种也重复，同一个循环覆盖到动植物。

senses.title: Special clothing of monks and nuns
senses.definition: the long loose garment worn by members of religious orders
senses.definitionCN: 修士修女穿着的宽松长袍
senses.example: The nun's black habit hung in the closet.
senses.exampleCN: 修女的黑色会服挂在衣柜里。
senses.why: Daily routine once included what a monk always wore, so the dress took the name of regularity.
senses.whyCN: 修士日复一日穿着同样的衣服，这种规律性让服装也借用了「习惯」之名。

senses.title: A custom shared by many
senses.definition: a practice common in a group or society
senses.definitionCN: 某个群体或社会中普遍的做法
senses.example: Tea at four is an old habit here.
senses.exampleCN: 四点喝茶是这里的旧例。
senses.why: When one person's loop becomes everyone's loop, habit widens into custom.
senses.whyCN: 一个人的循环变成大家的循环，习惯便扩大为风俗。

senses.title: Physical or mental constitution
senses.definition: the general physical or mental makeup of a person, as in slender habit
senses.definitionCN: 人的总体身体或心理特征，如 slender habit
senses.example: He has a nervous habit of mind.
senses.exampleCN: 他有神经质的脾性。
senses.why: Repeated states shape the whole person, so the loop leaves marks on constitution.
senses.whyCN: 反复出现的状态塑造整个人，循环在体质上留下印记。

intro.en: Habit began as the idea of having or holding, then slid into what one wears and does.
intro.cn: habit 始于「持有、拥有」的概念，继而滑向「穿着之物」与「惯常之事」。

items.en: Latin habere meant to have or hold, and habitus meant condition or state of holding oneself.
items.cn: 拉丁语 habere 意为拥有，habitus 意为状态、自身的持有方式。

items.en: Habitus also named style of dress, the way one holds clothes on the body.
items.cn: habitus 也指穿着样式，即衣物在身上的持法。

items.en: Old French habit meant clothing and later general custom.
items.cn: 古法语 habit 指服装，后来泛指习俗。

items.en: Middle English habit first meant dress, especially of religious orders.
items.cn: 中古英语 habit 最初指衣着，尤指修会服饰。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the repeated-action meaning dominated English habit.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，「反复行为」义在英语 habit 中占了主导。

note.cn: 与 habit 形近或义近的词。

definition_zh: 绿色的；未熟的；环保的；草地
definition_en: of the colour of grass, not yet ripe, or concerned with the environment
core_image: 一片刚修剪过的草地，草叶上的水珠映着阳光
scene: 雨后的草地一片鲜绿，叶尖上还挂着水珠。 The grass turned green after the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 green 是「绿色的」（第 01 个义项）；句意是雨后草变绿了。

pos.zh: 形容词：绿色的、未熟的、环保的

senses.title: The colour of growing grass
senses.definition: having the colour of grass and leaves
senses.definitionCN: 像草和树叶那样的颜色
senses.example: The grass turned green after the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 雨后草变绿了。
senses.why: Green goes back to Old English grēne, related to grow, and names the colour of things as they grow.
senses.whyCN: green 来自古英语 grēne，与 grow 同源，命名的是草木生长时的颜色。

senses.title: Not yet ripe
senses.definition: not yet ripe, said of fruit
senses.definitionCN: 果实还没有成熟
senses.example: The apples are still green.
senses.exampleCN: 苹果还是青的。
senses.why: Unripe fruit stays green instead of turning red or yellow, so the colour word also marks what is not ready to eat.
senses.whyCN: 没熟的果子不会转红转黄，仍保持青色，于是这个颜色词也标记「还不能吃」。

senses.title: Friendly to the environment
senses.definition: causing little harm to the environment
senses.definitionCN: 对环境损害很小
senses.example: The town buys green energy.
senses.exampleCN: 这个镇购买绿色能源。
senses.why: Growing plants stand for clean air and unspoiled land, so green became the label for things that protect nature.
senses.whyCN: 生长的植物代表干净的空气与未受破坏的土地，于是 green 成了保护自然的标签。

senses.title: Inexperienced
senses.definition: new to a job and without much experience
senses.definitionCN: 刚入行、缺乏经验
senses.example: A green recruit needs help on the first day.
senses.exampleCN: 新来的生手第一天需要人带。
senses.why: New shoots are green before they harden, so a person new to a job is called green.
senses.whyCN: 新枝在木质化之前也是青嫩的，所以刚做一份工作的人被叫作 green。

definition_en: in what way, by what method, or to what degree
core_image: 一个人站在岔路口，抬手指向两条不同的路
scene: 他站在岔路口，抬手指向两条不同的路。 How did you find the way?

senses.title: In what way
senses.definition: in what way or by what means
senses.definitionCN: 用什么方式、靠什么办法
senses.example: How did you find the way?
senses.exampleCN: 你是怎么找到路的？
senses.why: How goes back to Old English hū, the instrumental form of the word for 'who or what', so it asks 'by what means'.
senses.whyCN: how 来自古英语 hū，是表示「谁、什么」那个词的工具格，问的是「用什么手段」。

senses.title: To what degree
senses.definition: to what degree or extent
senses.definitionCN: 达到什么程度
senses.example: How tall is your brother?
senses.exampleCN: 你弟弟有多高？
senses.why: The same question word can measure an amount instead of a method, so how also asks about degree.
senses.whyCN: 同一个疑问词也能衡量数量而不是方法，所以 how 也问程度。

senses.title: In what condition, especially of health
senses.definition: in what condition, often asked about someone's health
senses.definitionCN: 处于什么状况，常用于问候健康
senses.example: How are you today?
senses.exampleCN: 你今天怎么样？
senses.why: Asking how a person is asks about the state they are in, which is why the word became the standard health greeting.
senses.whyCN: 问一个人 how，就是问他处在什么状态，所以这个词成了问候健康的标准说法。

definition_zh: 帽子；盖；帽状物；覆盖；上限
definition_en: a soft hat with a peak, a lid, or an upper limit
core_image: 一顶带檐的布帽扣在头上，帽檐压住眉线
scene: 门口的人把帽檐压低，挡住斜射进来的光。 He wore a blue cap to the game.
sceneCN: 这里 cap 是「帽子」（第 01 个义项）；句意是他戴着一顶蓝帽去看比赛。

derivatives.zh: 由 cap 加 -ed 构成，义为「有上限的」
由 cap 加 -ful 构成，义为「一帽之量」
由 cap 与 stone 复合，义为「顶石」

senses.title: A soft hat with a peak
senses.definition: a soft hat with a flat peak, worn on the head
senses.definitionCN: 有帽檐、戴在头上的软帽
senses.example: He wore a blue cap to the game.
senses.exampleCN: 他戴着一顶蓝帽去看比赛。
senses.why: Cap came through Latin cappa, 'head covering', and Old English cæppe, and the head-covering sense is its base.
senses.whyCN: cap 经拉丁语 cappa「头巾」和古英语 cæppe 而来，盖在头上的东西是它的本义。

senses.title: A lid or top for a container
senses.definition: a lid or covering for the top of a bottle or tube
senses.definitionCN: 瓶口或管口上的盖
senses.example: The bottle cap rolled under the table.
senses.exampleCN: 瓶盖滚到了桌子底下。
senses.why: A cap covers the head; a lid covers the top of a bottle, so the same word serves both coverings.
senses.whyCN: 帽子盖着头，瓶盖盖着瓶口，同一种「盖」的用法就用同一个词。

senses.title: An upper limit
senses.definition: a fixed upper limit on an amount or a price
senses.definitionCN: 数量或价格上封顶的界限
senses.example: The government set a cap on fuel prices.
senses.exampleCN: 政府给燃料价格设了上限。
senses.why: A cap seals the top so nothing can rise higher, and that picture became a limit on numbers.
senses.whyCN: 盖子封住顶端，东西再也不能往上冒，这个画面就变成了数字上的上限。

senses.title: To cover the top of something
senses.definition: to cover the top of something, as snow covers a hill
senses.definitionCN: 像雪盖住山顶那样盖在某物的顶部
senses.example: Snow capped the hills before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天亮前雪盖住了山冈。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb, so to cap a hill is to put a cap of snow or ice on it.
senses.whyCN: 名词转作动词，cap 一座山就是给它盖上一层雪或冰。

senses.title: To set an upper limit on something
senses.definition: to put a fixed upper limit on an amount or price
senses.definitionCN: 给数量或价格封顶
senses.example: The city capped the bus fare at two dollars.
senses.exampleCN: 市里把公交车费封顶在两美元。
senses.why: The limiting sense of the noun also became a verb: to cap a fare is to put a lid on how high it can go.
senses.whyCN: 名词的「上限」义也转成动词：cap a fare 就是给票价盖上一个盖子，不许再涨。

definition_en: moving or happening quickly, or done at high speed
core_image: 跑道上一个男孩冲刺，风把衣服吹得贴在身上
scene: 跑道上一个男孩冲刺，风把衣服吹得贴在身上。 He is a fast runner.

senses.title: Moving quickly
senses.definition: moving or happening quickly
senses.definitionCN: 移动或发生得很快
senses.example: He is a fast runner.
senses.exampleCN: 他跑得很快。
senses.why: Old English fæst meant firm or fixed; a runner who holds firmly to the ground could go at speed, and 'firm' turned into 'quick'.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 fæst 意为「牢固、固定」；跑者稳稳踏地才能跑得快，「牢固」由此转成「迅速」。

senses.title: Quick to learn
senses.definition: quick to learn or understand
senses.definitionCN: 理解得快
senses.example: She is a fast learner.
senses.exampleCN: 她学东西很快。
senses.why: The same speed sense is applied to the mind: a person who takes things in quickly is called fast, as in a fast learner.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「快」的意思用在头脑上：接受得快的人就叫 fast，如 a fast learner。

senses.title: At high speed
senses.definition: at high speed
senses.definitionCN: 以很快的速度
senses.example: The car runs fast on the highway.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车在高速路上跑得很快。
senses.why: English uses the same form as an adverb, so fast describes the speed of an action without adding -ly.
senses.whyCN: 英语直接用同一形式作副词，因此 fast 不加 -ly 就能描述动作的速度。
